shadows.name: paper

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: One emphasized save, add, or export action per decision area.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Routine actions such as Save draft and Move down.

components.name: Field
components.description: Visible label with a calm border, used throughout the editor and libraries.
components.css: .ds-field{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:6px;color:#27272a;font:500 12px/1.5 system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-field input{min-height:40px;padding:8px 10px;background:#fff;color:#27272a;border:1px solid #d4d4d8;border-radius:4px;font:12px/1.5 system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-field input:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #2563eb;outline-offset:3px}

components.name: Section Row
components.description: Selects a block in the right rail without making the paper itself editable.

components.name: Workspace Navigation
components.description: Quiet horizontal navigation to bulletin and shared-library screens.

narrative.overview: The application is a quiet workspace around a printable object. On desktop, the bulletin preview owns most of the viewport; controls live alongside it rather than covering it. The interface is light, neutral, compact, and task-oriented, with blue reserved for an active choice or primary action.
keyCharacteristics: A white two-spread document against a cool neutral canvas
Plain sans-serif editing UI against serif print content

rules.name: The Document-First Rule
rules.body: Keep the page visually dominant; UI accents should identify actions and state rather than compete with bulletin content.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Reserve elevation for the printable sheet and active dialogs; separate routine controls with spacing, tone, and fine borders.

dos: Do keep preview, edit controls, and save/generation status separately identifiable.
Do use the exact selected visual hierarchy as a starting point when building the real web application; see docs/design/EDITOR.md and reference captures.
Do surface broken references, overflow, and stale revisions with specific messages and a way back to the affected content.
donts: Don't turn the screen mockup's localStorage, HTML measurement, browser print, or fixture content into backend or PDF authority.
Don't lock branding or other blocks to the cover: the physical panel is fixed, its contents are not.
Don't introduce promotional banners, sidebar slogans, app footers, or click-to-edit behavior on the preview; the selected concept keeps editing in the sidebar.
